chunks: What the Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me of, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who passes by water in which there is a dead animal that has become putrid. He said: “If the foul odor predominates over the water, then he should not perform wudu (ablution) from it, nor should he drink.”

key_terms.أَنْتَنَتْ: it became putrid and emitted a bad smell
key_terms.الْمَاءِ: water under discussion for ritual and ordinary use
key_terms.دَابَّةٌ: a creature or animal found in the water

ai.seo_question: Can water be used for wudu (ablution) or drinking if a dead animal has rotted in it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning water contaminated by a dead creature. If the putrid smell has become dominant in the water, it is not to be used for wudu (ablution) or for drinking, indicating the legal effect of perceptible impurity upon water.
